title: Infra primitives consolidation rationale
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working rationale for consolidating several overlapping terraform modules and simplifying outputs/variables for private deployments (VPC / on-prem clusters across EKS/GKE/AKS). The immediate goal is not to ship a single-big-module but to reduce accidental surface area, make upgrades less risky, and provide clear migration hooks for downstream consumers (customer-side infra, onboarding scripts, and our cluster factory).

Principles: (short)
- explicit minimal outputs: expose only what other modules truly consume
- stable names first: breaking changes should be gated behind major version bumps + migration scripts
- idempotent interfaces: variables and outputs must be safe to call repeatedly in fresh and existing state
- migration friendliness: provide boomerang compatibility layers (shadow outputs, translational maps) 
- testing-in-prod mindset: smoke tests + canary clusters before org-wide rollout

Observed problems motivating consolidation:
- many small modules expose a large surface of outputs that are only used during onboarding; later consumers read the same values and become fragile when we rename outputs during refactors.
- duplicated logic for defaulting VPC CIDRs, secondary subnets, and tagging rules across cloud modules.
- IAM bindings spread across ecs/eks/cluster modules and service modules; difficult to reason about least privilege during upgrades.
- module inputs use inconsistent naming (e.g., vpc_subnet_ids vs private_subnet_ids vs subnet_ids) which forces fragile wrapper modules.
- existing upgrade scripts expect outputs in exact names; we currently rely on ad-hoc migration helpers (scripts in repo) and manual DBA/checklist steps.

High-level consolidation approach:
1) Split responsibilities by stable responsibility boundaries: network (vpc, subnets, nat/gateway), identity (iam roles/policies and role-attachments), cluster (eks/gke/aks bootstrap + nodepool glue)
2) Provide a single, tiny public facade module for each responsibility that downstreams import. Internally the facade can compose smaller primitives but only publish a very small set of outputs.
3) Define canonical variable names and mark aliases for backward compatibility. Each module will accept both canonical name and common legacy alias (with deprecation warnings logged by pre-apply scripts).
4) Introduce a compatibility_outputs map: when performing an upgrade, modules will create additional outputs that mirror legacy output names for one release window (two minor releases), then remove them after downstreams migrate.
5) Add an outputs-stability table to each module README (machine and human readable) documenting when outputs were introduced and a recommended migration path.

Proposed canonical variable/output sets (examples):
- vpc module public facade variables (canonical): vpc_cidr, private_subnet_cidrs, public_subnet_cidrs, azs, tags
- vpc module public facade outputs (canonical): vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, route_table_ids, main_route_table_id
- iam module variables: iam_prefix, service_account_mappings (list of maps), kms_key_arns (optional)
- iam module outputs: primary_role_arn, service_account_role_map (json string for terraform consumers), iam_policy_attachments (list)
- cluster module variables: cluster_name, kubernetes_version, node_pools (list of maps), vpc_id (canonically the vpc module output), subnet_ids (canonical: private_subnet_ids), iam_role_arns (canonical: primary_role_arn)
- cluster module outputs: cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert, cluster_oidc_provider_arn, node_group_ids

Naming compatibility pattern (implementation detail):
- Each module will accept a locals block that resolves alias variables. Example: locals { private_subnet_ids_resolved = coalesce(var.private_subnet_ids, var.vpc_subnet_ids, []) }
- Then outputs will be published under canonical names and an optional legacy_outputs object will be created conditional on var.publish_legacy_outputs (default true for one release window).

Upgrade and migration plan (practical steps):
- Phase 0: audit
  - run a TF plan scanner across repos to enumerate referenced outputs/variables (GH search + repo-level terraform graph) -> produce a mapping table: legacy_name -> modules/consumers. Target date: 2 weeks.
- Phase 1: introduce aliases and deprecation notices
  - ship facade modules that accept aliases but continue to publish legacy names under publish_legacy_outputs = true
  - publish migration README and slack announcement in #priv-deploys
  - add CI check that warns when PRs reference deprecated names
- Phase 2: canary rollouts
  - pick 2 non-critical customer clusters (internal staging + a partner test account) and upgrade modules with publish_legacy_outputs=true and additional smoke test harness (create cluster, validate kubeconfig, run sample workloads)
  - keep a monitoring dashboard for 48h, check for failed applies or drift
- Phase 3: signal and deprecate
  - after successful canaries, open deprecation window (30–60 days) with repeated reminders and an automated fixer script (Terraform import + state mv helpers)
- Phase 4: cleanup release
  - release a version that sets publish_legacy_outputs=false and removes legacy outputs entirely. Provide a migration helper repo tag that consumers can run to move state or rename references.

Testing matrix and automation notes:
- unit: terraform validate + tflint + terratest for small components (vpc module smoke).
- integration: end-to-end cluster creation across three cloud flavors (eks/gke/aks) using the facade module with canonical variables. Use ephemeral accounts and clean up.
- upgrade tests: run a staged pipeline that performs an in-place upgrade from previous module version to new version in a test tenancy; include state mv operations (terraform state mv) where needed and assert resource ids stable (no recreation)
- canary rollback: pipeline must capture the last working state snapshot and be able to re-apply previous module version state. Maintain automated snapshots of tfstate for 72 hours after change.

Backward-compatibility patterns and pitfalls to avoid:
- Avoid conditional renaming of resources based on variable values (this causes resource replacement). Instead, prefer stable resource names and create thin wrapper resources if necessary.
- Refrain from changing resource types (e.g., aws_iam_role -> aws_iam_role with different lifecycle) without a migration plan and explicit state move commands.
- Do not collapse multiple outputs into a single map in the same release where consumers expect scalar outputs; if you must, publish both types and mark the map as canonical in a planned deprecation window.

Testing checklist for module maintainers (to include in PR template):
- [ ] audit of direct and indirect consumers (list attached)
- [ ] local plan shows no resource replacements for consumer resources
- [ ] module has publish_legacy_outputs toggles and true by default while in deprecation window
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry and README updates for outputs stability table
- [ ] terratest integration executed and passed in CI

Operational runbooks and quick commands (notes):
- Terraform state rename helper (example): terraform state mv module.old_module.aws_subnet.private[0] module.new_module.aws_subnet.private[0]  -- run from CI runner with tfenv pinned to supported version.
- Quick check for deprecated output usage across repos: gh api graphql -F query='search(query: "private_subnet_ids in:repo", type: CODE, first: 100) { ... }'
- Debugging guidance: if cluster creation fails after module upgrade, check for: missing OIDC provider, mismatched subnet counts, IAM role assume policy errors. Typical fixes: enable publish_legacy_outputs, re-run state mv, or roll back to previous module version.

Open questions (for design review):
- Should publish_legacy_outputs default to true or should it be an opt-in at first? My leaning: default true for one release window, then flip at cleanup release.
- How long should we keep alias variables resolved in modules? 2 minor releases seems adequate but gets fuzzy for long-lived private clusters.
- Are there internal tools/consumers (solutions-engineering scripts) that embed outputs in SQL/monitoring dashboards that we need to coordinate with? (action: run repo search)

Next steps and owners:
- Audit scan: Ibrahim to run repo search + produce mapping (due 2024-11-05)
- Prototype facade module for vpc: Samir to author and include alias resolution and publish_legacy_outputs toggle (due 2024-11-19)
- Terratest suites: Maya to convert existing cluster smoke tests into reusable pipeline jobs (due 2024-12-03)
- Communications: Lena to draft and post migration plan on Confluence and #priv-deploys (due 2024-11-12)

Notes to self / working reminders:
- keep variable examples short in README but include long-form examples in examples/ directory (one example per cloud provider)
- consider adding a lightweight lifecycle "stable_output" tag in README that tools can scrape
- look at past incident PD-201 for example of output renaming fallout

Appendix: example minimal vpc facade variables and outputs (for README)
variables:
- name: vpc_cidr (string)
- name: private_subnet_cidrs (list(string))
- name: azs (list(string))
- name: tags (map(string), optional)

outputs:
- name: vpc_id (string)
- name: private_subnet_ids (list(string))
- name: public_subnet_ids (list(string))
- name: route_table_ids (list(string))

End of note.
